name: e-ASTROGAM / All-Sky-ASTROGAM
full_name: enhanced ASTROGAM and All-Sky-ASTROGAM mission concepts
summary: e-ASTROGAM is proposed for low Earth orbit, while All-Sky-ASTROGAM is proposed for Sun–Earth L2. They are grouped here as a related concept family; the two designs have different geometries, energy ranges and orbits.
detection_principle: Combines Compton-scattering and pair-conversion imaging to measure low-energy gamma-ray continua, narrow lines, polarization and spatial distributions, helping separate dark-matter signals from Galactic foregrounds / pulsars.

results.summary: The white paper describes potential for WIMP, positron and Galactic-background studies; no flight data.
Independent model studies assess the sensitivity of future telescopes including e-ASTROGAM to nuclear-absorption gamma-ray lines from dark matter at about 10–30 MeV.

science_scope: Searches cosmic gamma-ray, antiparticle or neutrino spectra, directions and fluxes for indirect signatures of dark-matter annihilation, decay or related new physics. Conventional astrophysical sources and propagation can produce similar signals, requiring background modeling; design sensitivity is not a measured limit or discovery.
